dedupe_keys.name: gcam china global change analysis model with provincial breakout for china

description: GCAM-China is a version of the Global Change Analysis Model (GCAM) that splits China's energy-economic system into 31 provincial sub-regions and six electricity grid regions while staying embedded in the global model. It is developed and maintained jointly by the Center for Global Sustainability at the University of Maryland, the College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering and the Institute of Carbon Neutrality at Peking University, and the Department of Earth System Science and the Institute for Carbon Neutrality at Tsinghua University, with a model documentation paper led by S. Xu. Version 6 was built on GCAM 6 with selected GCAM 7 updates and added electricity by power segment, a detailed China-specific industry sector, and rural and urban residential buildings; versions 7, 7.1 and 8 followed. Coverage is China by province within a global model. The code is accessible on GitHub under the Educational Community License 2.0 and releases are downloadable from Zenodo, at no cost, with a manual and getting-started guide online. Caveats: the Zenodo record states CC BY 4.0 while the repository licence file is ECL 2.0, and running GCAM needs substantial setup. Simulation uses are long-term provincial energy transition, power sector and emissions scenarios for China. Related records: none linked on the provider's pages read on the day.
